## README.md
**One brain for you and your company, read by every agent you use.** Put your own notes and your company's docs in one place: a facts page, a decisions log, call transcripts. Claude Code, Codex and your other agents look there before they answer, so they stop starting from zero and work from what you and your team actually wrote down.
GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host, and it starts with no API keys: search is by keyword until you add one. gbrain.io is optional paid hosting.
Tip
**Need hosted? First time running an agent?** Try **[gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/?ref=readme)** , hosted GBrain, for the easiest experience: one brain for you and your team, connected to ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor, with nothing to install or keep online. Stuck? Email [support@gbrain.io](mailto:support@gbrain.io) and a person will set it up with you, free.

...

* Every new Claude Code or Codex session looks in your brain before it answers, without being told to.
* Anything you ask your agent to remember is still there in the next session, in every agent connected to the brain.
* Your notes and your company's docs are searchable, and your agent answers questions like _"what did we decide about pricing, and why?"_ from them.

...

| How it connects | Agents |

| MCP from its guide | [ChatGPT](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/mcp/CHATGPT.md) , [Claude Desktop](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/mcp/CLAUDE_DESKTOP.md) , [Claude Cowork](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/mcp/CLAUDE_COWORK.md) , [Perplexity](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/mcp/PERPLEXITY.md) , [Grok Build](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/mcp/GROK.md) , [Grok Bot](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/grok-bot.md) , [Muse](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/muse.md) , Windsurf and other stdio clients |
| Any other coding agent | Paste the install prompt below |

...

## Install
Tip
**Fastest: hosted GBrain at [gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/cli?ref=readme) , for any harness.** One command launches a GBrain hosted on gbrain.io; Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor and every other AI you use connect to it, with nothing to keep online.
```shell
curl -sSL https://gbrainio.terminalwire.sh | bash
gbrainio terminal connect      # in a new terminal
gbrainio workspace new         # pick a plan in the browser
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash   # skip if Bun 1.4.4+ is installed
export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"
bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain   # the gbrain CLI only; no local brain
# Claude Code (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
(claude mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || claude mcp add --transport http --scope user gbrain https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup claude-code --instructions-only
# Codex (an existing gbrain entry is kept):
(codex mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || codex mcp add gbrain --url https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup codex --instructions-only
```
`gbrain setup <harness> --instructions-only` tells the agent the brain is there; agents seldom call an MCP server nobody told them about. It writes the [brain-first block](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/setup.md) into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or Codex's `AGENTS.md` (a non-empty `AGENTS.override.md` instead when Codex has one) with a per-turn rule hook, and leaves the MCP entry alone; the same command with `--no-instructions` added takes them out.

...

### Here's how to self-host it
GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host. It needs **Bun 1.4.4 or newer** ; existing worker installs read the [authorization and queue upgrade guide](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/authorization-upgrade.md) before restarting on this version.

...

**GBrain is NOT distributed on npm.** The npm `gbrain` package is unrelated and
can shadow the real binary, so never run `npm install -g gbrain` or `bun add -g gbrain` . Install only via `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain` (the soaked stable channel; `` is the alpha line with every release)
or `git clone --branch stable` + `bun install && bun link` . Installed by mistake? `gbrain doctor` gives the fix.

...

### Add your notes and your company's docs
Then open a new agent session and ask _"What did we decide about a free plan, and why?"_ : the answer comes from your decisions log. `--federated` puts the folder in default search, and `--force` accepts a folder that isn't a git repository; in a folder that is one, GBrain reads only committed files, so commit your edits before you sync.
To see the shape first, `gbrain sources demo company-brain` runs a fictional company in a few seconds without touching your brain. Before you share a company brain with a team, read the [company-brain tutorial](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/tutorials/company-brain.md) .
GBrain is not a data warehouse or analytics store. Keep ads, analytics, CRM and payment data in your warehouse, and connect your agent to it separately.

...

### Connect GBrain to your AI client (MCP)
* **This brain from anywhere:** `gbrain mcp expose` publishes it on your Tailscale tailnet as a user service ( `--funnel` for cloud agents such as Grok Bot, Muse and ChatGPT). [Guide](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/remote-mcp.md) .
* **A brain on another host:** `gbrain connect https://your-host/mcp --token gbrain_xxx --install` (add `--agent codex` for Codex).
Hosted brains use [native OAuth or a private handoff](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/hosted-harness-access.md) ; dashboard, clients and permissions live in [MCP administration](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/mcp/ADMIN.md) .

...

**Keep skills beside knowledge.** New local brains include memory skills in their
content root. Agents can join an authorized catalog; only approved editors can
publish. Managed coding-agent installs add an owned native router; restart and
real-use verification are separate steps. Staged migration preserves sharing
choices and personal edits.

...

## Choose your setup
**Use the brain on my own computer from everywhere.** One command publishes it over MCP on your Tailscale tailnet and keeps it running: `gbrain mcp expose` (add `--funnel` for cloud agents such as Grok Bot, Muse and ChatGPT). Follow **[use your brain from anywhere over MCP](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/remote-mcp.md)** . **Say to your agent:** _"use my brain over mcp"_ — _"put my brain on tailscale"_ .
3.

...

I'm Garry Tan, President and CEO of Y Combinator. I built GBrain to run my own AI agents. It's the production brain behind my OpenClaw and Hermes deployments: **155,795 pages, 24,589 people, 5,340 companies** , 66 cron jobs running autonomously. My agent ingests meetings, emails, tweets, voice calls, and original ideas while I sleep. It enriches every person and company it encounters. It fixes its own citations and consolidates memory overnight.

...

The point of building a 150K-page brain is to use it as a strategic moat. To never lose context. To query what's in your own head without re-reading it. The brain layer is what makes the moat usable. The 24/7 dream cycle is what keeps it sharp. Both run on your hardware, your DB, your keys.
It's easier to ship a daemon that runs 24/7 to ingest, enrich, and consolidate than it is to keep an agent in chat working hard. GBrain is that daemon, generalized. Install in 30 minutes. Your agent does the work. As my personal agent gets smarter, so does yours.

...

> **LLMs:** fetch [`llms.txt`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/llms.txt) for the documentation map, or [`llms-full.txt`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/llms-full.txt) for the same map with core docs inlined in one fetch. **Agents:** start with [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/AGENTS.md) (or [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/CLAUDE.md) if you're Claude Code).

...

## What this looks like
Five pages you now have to open and read yourself to actually prepare. The tool found the right material, but it didn't do the work.
**GBrain gives you back the answer, with sources:**

...

## Two ways to query your brain
**`gbrain think`** runs the same retrieval, then composes a synthesized answer across the results with explicit citations to the source pages AND an honest note on what the brain doesn't know yet. The gap analysis is the differentiator: the answer tells you when a page is stale, when a claim is uncited, when two pages contradict each other, when there's a hole you should fill.

...

**Why it compounds.** Pair the brain layer with `find_trajectory` and you get answers like _"how have the company's metrics changed AND what does the team look like right now AND what did they promise / share AND when did we last meet AND what's the value-add I can offer here"_ : well-scored, well-cited, in one shot. That's the strategic moat. That's why building a 150K-page brain is worth the effort.

...

## How to get data in
**Say to your agent:** _"Remember this with its source"_ — _"What should I import first?"_
[Data ingestion guide](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/data-ingestion.md) covers files, conversations, connectors, Google data, and capture commands.

## Your brain's shape (schema packs)
Most personal-knowledge tools force one fixed layout: their idea of "notes" + "people" + "tags." Drop a Notion export or your own years-old Obsidian vault on top, and the agent doesn't know what a `Projects/` folder means or whether `Reading/` is people or sources.
**gbrain doesn't have a fixed layout.** It ships with bundled schema packs and lets you author your own when none fit:
* **`gbrain-base-v2`** (default) — 15-type DRY/MECE canonical taxonomy (14 canonical + `note` catch-all): `person` , `company` , `media` , `tweet` , `social-digest` , `analysis` , `atom` , `concept` , `source` , `deal` , `email` , `slack` , `writing` , `project` , `note` . Subtypes/format/origin pushed to frontmatter.
* **`gbrain-base`** (legacy) — the wider 24-type layout.
Stays bundled for back-compat; brains on it can upgrade via `gbrain onboard --check --explain` → `gbrain jobs submit unify-types --params '{"target_pack":"gbrain-base-v2","apply":true}'` (omit `"apply":true` for a dry-run preview — that is the default).
* **`gbrain-recommended`** — extends `gbrain-base` with the 13 additional directories from `docs/GBRAIN_RECOMMENDED_SCHEMA.md` (source, place, trip, conversation, personal, civic, project, etc.).

...

The active pack threads through every read + write path: `parseMarkdown` infers page type from the pack's path prefixes; `whoknows` scopes expert routing to types declared `expert_routing: true` ; `extract_facts` runs only on `extractable: true` types. The retained search-cache key includes the pack name + version, but semantic result reuse is temporarily disabled. Switch packs and the brain re-interprets itself; switch back and nothing's lost.
Seven-tier resolution chain (per-call flag → env var → per-source DB key → brain-wide DB key → `gbrain.yml` → `~/.gbrain/config.json` → `gbrain-base` default). Full reference + authoring guide: [`docs/architecture/schema-packs.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/architecture/schema-packs.md) .

...

## Tutorials
* [**Set up your personal AI agent + brain from zero**](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/tutorials/personal-brain.md) — the canonical full-stack install. Two GitHub repos, a Telegram bot, AlphaClaw on Render, OpenClaw + GBrain + Supabase. End-to-end in about 2 hours.

...

## What it does (the loop)
```
  signal   →   search   →   respond   →   write   →   auto-link   →   sync
  (every    (brain-first  (informed     (page +    (typed edges     (cron
  message)  retrieval)    by context)   timeline)  + backlinks)     keeps fresh)
```
* **Signal detector** , after you opt in, captures durable ideas and entity mentions from substantive messages. Explicit remembering works without automatic capture; paid enrichment is a separate choice.
* **Brain-first lookup** before any external API call. The cheapest, fastest, most personal information source you have.
* **Auto-link** extracts graph links for trusted local page writes.
No LLM calls; pure pattern matching on page references such as `[[people/alice-example]]` . Unresolved extracted facts keep their provenance without inventing a backing page.
* **Cron-driven enrichment** runs while you sleep: dedup people pages, fix citations, score salience, find contradictions, prep tomorrow's tasks.
The whole loop is described in [`docs/architecture/topologies.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/architecture/topologies.md) with diagrams.
**Say to your agent:** _"Did upkeep run?"_ (your agent's open `gbrain serve` runs the free upkeep while it is idle; `gbrain maintain --schedule` adds a timer for a brain no agent opens) — _"Run dream"_ — _"Did the dream cycle run?"_

## Capabilities
GBrain combines keyword and semantic retrieval, typed graph traversal, optional cited synthesis, background jobs, and curated agent skills.

...

## Integrations
* **Rerankers** : Voyage `rerank-3-lite` hosted (the default unless `search.reranker.model` is set; on in `balanced` and `tokenmax` , same `VOYAGE_API_KEY` as embeddings; `gbrain config set search.reranker.model voyage:rerank-2.5` restores the previous default), plus the `llama-server-reranker` recipe for fully-local cross-encoder rerank via llama.cpp running Qwen3-Reranker against the same `gateway.rerank()` seam.

...

## Architecture
```
flowchart LR
    Repo[Markdown brain repos] --> Sync[Sync and parse]
    Sync --> Engine{Brain engine}
    Engine -->|default| PGLite[(PGLite)]
    Engine -->|shared or large| Postgres[(Postgres and pgvector)]
    Agent[AI agent or operator] --> Surface[CLI or MCP]
    Surface --> Ops[Contract-first operations]
    Ops --> Search[Hybrid retrieval]
    Ops --> Graph[Typed graph traversal]
    PGLite --> Search
    Postgres --> Search
    PGLite --> Graph
    Postgres --> Graph
    Search --> Synthesis[Synthesis and gap analysis]
    Graph --> Synthesis
    Synthesis --> Answer[Cited answer]
```

...

**Two engines, one contract.** PGLite (Postgres 17 via WASM, zero-config, default) for personal brains up to ~50K pages. Postgres + pgvector (Supabase or self-hosted) for shared, large or multi-machine brains. Both implement one `BrainEngine` contract ( [`src/core/engine.ts`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/src/core/engine.ts) ); CLI and MCP share one op registry.

...

DB-only pages, unresolved facts, history and operational state need a database backup: [where your memory lives](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/where-your-memory-lives.md) , [system of record](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/architecture/system-of-record.md) . Publish public subsets, share team mounts, or point a thin client at a colleague's brain.

...

**Two organizational axes (brain ⊥ source).** A _brain_ is a database (your personal brain, a team mount you joined). A _source_ is a repo inside that brain. Routing uses `.gbrain-source` dotfiles and a 6-tier precedence chain. Diagrams in [`docs/architecture/brains-and-sources.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/architecture/brains-and-sources.md) .
**Why the graph matters.** Vector search finds similar text; graph retrieval follows stored relationships. Extracted edges are evidence to inspect, not proof that a relationship is true. Graph freshness depends on the write path and maintenance described in [memory boundaries](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/memory-boundaries.md) .
Deep dive: [retrieval architecture](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/architecture/RETRIEVAL.md) ; [entity recall](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/entity-recall.md) .

...

## Docs
* [Anatomy of a page](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/page-anatomy.md) — frontmatter, timeline, facts; [per-client facts](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/entity-scoped-facts.md)
* [`docs/what-schemas-unlock.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/what-schemas-unlock.md) — why schemas matter: 7 killer use cases, the structural argument for typed page kinds, the agent-co-curates pattern
* [`docs/schema-author-tutorial.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/schema-author-tutorial.md) — 5-minute walkthrough: fork the bundled pack, add a custom type, backfill existing pages, prove the wiring via `gbrain whoknows`
* [`docs/architecture/`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/architecture) — system design, topologies, retrieval theory
* [`docs/guides/`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides) — how-to runbooks (google connect, open loops, sub-agent routing, minion deployment, skill development, brain-first lookup, idea capture, diligence ingestion)
* [`docs/integrations/`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/integrations) — connecting external data sources (voice, email, calendar, embedding providers)

...

* [Evals](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/eval) and [research](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/research) — methods and results
* [`docs/ethos/`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/ethos) — philosophy (thin harness, fat skills, markdown as recipes, origin story)
* [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/AGENTS.md) — entry point for non-Claude agents
* [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/CLAUDE.md) — entry point for Claude Code (deep operating context)
* [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) — contributor guide, test discipline, eval-capture mode
* [`SECURITY.md`](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/SECURITY.md) — install-path trust model, self-update integrity, automated scanning, OAuth threat model, hardening defaults

...

59:The rule: an important fix reaches stable within a day once it has passed the full test suite and the load test in step 2; everything else rides a weekly move; and stable never sits more than seven days behind tested changes. The scheduled check can move it at most twice a day; a maintainer can also promote, or roll back, by hand. {"output": "## Pinning a version

Install an exact release tag with this command. Its first line checks that the tag exists. Its second line removes any gbrain Bun already has installed, because installing one tag over another can leave the old version running and damage Bun's global package list. Its third line installs the tag:

```bash
git ls-remote --exit-code --tags https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain refs/tags/v<version> >/dev/null && \
  { ! bun pm ls -g 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'gbrain@' || bun remove -g gbrain; } && \
  bun add -g --backend=copyfile github:garrytan/gbrain#v<version>
```

Replace `<version>` with a release number, for example `0.60.722.0`. The second line skips the removal when Bun has no gbrain installed, so the same command works on a machine that never had gbrain.

A tag-pinned install stays on that release through `bun update`. `gbrain upgrade` is what moves it, so don't run it while you want to stay put. To stop update checks and update notices as well:

```bash
gbrain config set self_upgrade.mode off
```
